cells.question: Q03
cells.note: The text names FAIF, but its bibliography labels [xAI, 2025] “xai risk management framework” without an edition-specific date or address. Because the names differ and the year fits multiple 2025 documents, no edition is inferred.

search.read: §1, bibliography and all PDF link annotations

cells.question: Q04

cells.question: Q05
cells.note: The card names its framework (§1) and refers to the model’s “capability threshold” without stating which threshold or outcome in the framework’s categories: a determination referred to without its outcome. The conclusions on cybersecurity and manipulation risk (§§4.2.2–4.3.2) are stated as risk views, not in the framework’s categories, and no chemical or biological outcome category is given.

search.read: Whole card, especially §§1.3, 3.3 and 4.1–4.3 and bibliography

setAside.reason: Conclusions about cybersecurity and manipulation risks do not state outcomes in the framework’s own categories.

passages.quote: We release Grok 4.20 with safeguards appropriate for its capability threshold, such as refusal training.

crossFamily.result: material disagreement, decided: the checker read partly (blind), because §1.3 refers to the model’s capability threshold under the framework the card names without stating which, the criterion’s case of a determination made without stating its outcome. The pack had read not found. The maintainer decided for partly (decision a, 2026-11-05).

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: We release Grok 4.20 with safeguards appropriate for its capability threshold, such as refusal training.

cells.note: The card names refusal training, but does not identify a reached/not-reached framework threshold or a determination to which it is tied.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: We assess Grok 4.20’s dual-use capabilities, i.e., its ability to enable harm.

cells.note: §§4–4.1 report chemical and biological evaluations and benchmark results, without a domain outcome category or threshold determination. Technical benchmark contents and scores are not recorded.

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: we do not believe that it substantially increases cybersecurity risk.

cells.note: The card states this conclusion after its offensive-cyber capability evaluation. It is not a framework category determination.

cells.question: Q09
cells.note: No passage meeting the criterion was found in the recorded search.

setAside.reason: Open-ended introspective statements about self-modification or propagation are not capability evaluations of autonomy.
Agentic cyber evaluation does not independently establish self-replication, self-improvement or AI R&D evaluation.

cells.question: Q10

passages.quote: we do not believe that it poses significant risks due to advanced persuasion capabilities.

cells.note: The card gives this conclusion for a manipulation benchmark with another model as defender. It does not report persuasion effects on human participants.

cells.question: Q11

passages.quote: Grok 4.20 occasionally acts against operator interests when given extensive affordances and confronted with evidence of egregious harm

cells.note: The card reports this conditional sabotage-audit finding. It is not a claim about the frequency of such behaviour in ordinary use.

cells.question: Q12

cells.note: The card reports third-party red-teaming of an early checkpoint, scoped to the refusal boundary and catastrophic risk.

cells.question: Q13

passages.quote: we provided third-party evaluators access to an early snapshot of Grok 4.20 for testing of our refusal policy.

cells.note: The external evaluators are described without organisation names; the snapshot is early, rather than necessarily the final deployed model.
